Last month, OpenAI previewed a hardware product under the Codex brand. Today, the company officially announced that the Codex Micro keyboard, developed in collaboration with Work Louder, is now on sale, priced at US$230.

Here's a product introduction:

This keyboard is offered in two versions: a tactile click version (blue switch, audible) and a silent version.

According to the official website: "Each Agent key displays RGB lighting effects based on Codex's real-time status, so you can tell at a glance whether it's thinking, executing, waiting, or already done — without having to switch conversation windows first."

The product page also lists three Codex-exclusive features:

  • Instant skill activation: flick the joystick to launch common Codex workflows, such as reviewing pull requests, debugging, or refactoring code.
  • Core actions at your fingertips: dedicated shortcut keys for the most common operations, including accepting, rejecting, talking back, opening new conversations, and more. Less switching, faster delivery.
  • Real-time compute adjustment: twist the knob to adjust the reasoning level on the fly. Keep things fast on simple tasks, then crank it up when deep thinking is required.

You can order it right now. Here's a video as well:

That's about it. It's been quite a busy month for OpenAI and the hardware scene.
